# PB-04 bounded lookahead experiment

The experiment remains isolated. None of its three modes met the unchanged
25 ms event-admission budget. Production storage and the public engine are
unchanged; PB-04 remains open.

The existing batched prototype fetches one fresh proof frontier per SQL call.
Two candidate modes let PostgreSQL follow two additional levels of references
and return candidate bytes in the same call. Each query starts from at most128
roots and returns at most4096 nodes. Rust still verifies hashes, canonical bytes
and expected edge metadata. SQL results never establish absence or authority.
The existing transaction-local byte/node limits remain in force; this is not a
hard PostgreSQL or process-memory guarantee.

Broad lookahead follows map edges and value links. That reduces query count,
but it also reads unrequested opaque history arrays. Its fetched-byte growth
undermines the intended bounded working-set path. Map-only lookahead excludes
those value links, retaining the required read-set boundary while fetching more
map structure. Neither variant is selected by default.

Speculative neighbors may contain malformed JSON, invalid UTF-8 or altered
canonical bytes. Such neighbors are not cached as verified data. A later required
edge fetch must fail normally, and a full audit still detects unrelated damage.
This preserves the prototype's existing distinction between required-path checks
and a full-history audit. The first development attempt incorrectly widened that
integrity scope and failed the existing test; its evidence is retained.

The final three modes use source082881d and identical release binaries. Each
executes96 admissions,16 named correctness checks and four cold full audits.
All96 canonical state hashes and byte counts match across all three modes and
the existing full reference engine. Strict example Clippy passed. These are
sequential measurements on a shared host, not randomized or isolated speedup
claims. Raw samples, source inventories, database settings and process costs
are retained in `PB-04.lookahead.json` and its evidence directory.

| Retained history | Batched p95 ms | Map-only p95 ms | Broad p95 ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 50.774 | 62.532 | 49.698 |
| 32 | 56.512 | 66.771 | 52.660 |
| 128 | 60.201 | 81.272 | 60.389 |
| 512 | 64.251 | 77.710 | 77.156 |

At history512, mean SQL read calls fall from66 to50.96 with map-only lookahead
and34.96 with broad lookahead. Mean fetched bytes increase from85,523 to107,445
and278,197 respectively. Reducing round trips alone did not satisfy the budget.
No performance cell is discarded and no limit is raised.

A next experiment should address the fine-grained representation and repeated
canonical-planner work, with the same full-reference comparison. A production
implementation still needs a reviewed working-set planner API, actual namespace
ownership, protected storage, migration/full-CAS compatibility, physical bounds
and garbage collection. This experiment supplies none of those capabilities.
